name: create
title: Create a sandbox
description: Start a sandbox and wait until SSH answers; returns its name, CID, and TTL. With wait, a create the host's limits refuse queues for capacity first.

base.description: base to boot: nixos, nixos-gui, a prepared cloud base, or a Windows base that base_list reports

wait.description: queue up to this long, such as 30m, when the host's sandbox limits are full

gui.description: the base's GUI variant, with more default memory

name: run
title: Run a command in a one-shot sandbox
description: Create a sandbox, copy inputs to /root/ (C:\sbx\ on Windows), run the command, copy outputs out, and destroy the sandbox even when a step fails; returns {sandbox, phases, in, exec, out, cleanup, failure}, with exec shaped as the exec tool's result. A failed copy in, a transport error, a failed copy out, or a failed cleanup is a tool error with code run-incomplete whose run field holds that whole document, so exec still carries the command's result. With wait, a run the host's limits refuse queues for capacity first.

base.description: base to boot: nixos, nixos-gui, a prepared cloud base, or a Windows base that base_list reports

wait.description: queue up to this long, such as 30m, when the host's sandbox limits are full

gui.description: the base's GUI variant, with more default memory

in.description: host paths copied into /root/ or C:\sbx\

timeout.description: command timeout such as 10m; then SIGTERM, and SIGKILL 5 s later

cwd.description: absolute guest directory; default the user's home

env.description: variables set after the guest profile

encoding.description: stdout and stderr as text, with *_lossy set where invalid UTF-8 was replaced, or as base64 of the raw bytes; default text

stdin.description: text fed to the command's stdin, up to 1 MiB

stdin_base64.description: bytes fed to the command's stdin, base64, up to 1 MiB

command.description: argv of the guest command, run without a shell; wrap pipes in sh -c

annotations.title: Run a command in a one-shot sandbox

name: exec
title: Run a command in a sandbox
description: Run a command through the guest agent; returns {exit_code, signal, timed_out, killed, transport_error, duration_s, stdout, stderr, stdout_lossy, stderr_lossy, truncated}. A failing guest command is no tool error: exit_code is its status, or null with signal set when a signal ended it. timed_out means the timeout passed and sbx sent SIGTERM, then SIGKILL; transport_error means the guest agent stopped answering mid-command. The command runs as root in /root with HOME=/root unless user, cwd, or env say otherwise; Windows takes none of the three.

timeout.description: command timeout such as 10m; then SIGTERM, and SIGKILL 5 s later

cwd.description: absolute guest directory; default the user's home

env.description: variables set after the guest profile

encoding.description: stdout and stderr as text, with *_lossy set where invalid UTF-8 was replaced, or as base64 of the raw bytes; default text

stdin.description: text fed to the command's stdin, up to 1 MiB

stdin_base64.description: bytes fed to the command's stdin, base64, up to 1 MiB

command.description: argv of the guest command, run without a shell; wrap pipes in sh -c

annotations.title: Run a command in a sandbox

name: cp
title: Copy between host and sandbox
description: Copy a file or directory; one side is <name>:<path>. Without a destination a copy out lands in the sandbox's xfer directory; copies out never overwrite.

name: destroy
title: Destroy sandboxes
description: Stop and delete one sandbox, every sandbox of this agent session, or every expired one; give exactly one of name, mine, and expired. Returns the destroyed names.

mine.description: sandboxes of this agent session and its subagents

name: list
title: List sandboxes
description: Describe every sandbox: state, base, CID, TTL left, session, and xfer directory; creates waiting for capacity follow with state queued and their position.

mine.description: only sandboxes of this agent session and its subagents

name: info
title: Describe a sandbox
description: Describe one sandbox as list does, adding its console log, its base image, and shares: [{tag, read_only, host_path, mountpoint}] for each share it holds, with mountpoint only where the guest mounted it.

name: screenshot
title: Capture a sandbox display
description: Return the display as a PNG image content block alongside its saved path and MIME type. Each capture gets its own file in the sandbox's xfer directory, which destroy removes, or under 'to', which keeps it. Set ocr to also return the text tesseract reads in the text field.

to.description: host directory, or a new file, for the image; default the xfer directory

name: key
title: Press keys in a sandbox
description: Press each key or chord in turn on the display of a sandbox with a GUI base; returns {sandbox, keys}.

keys.description: keys or chords such as enter or ctrl+alt+t, pressed in turn

name: type
title: Type text in a sandbox
description: Type text on the display of a sandbox with a GUI base; returns {sandbox, characters}. By default xdotool types it in the X session as the user sbx, Unicode included and whatever the Caps Lock state; newline presses enter, and other control characters are refused. Mode keys sends US-layout keycodes from the host instead, for screens before X starts; it refuses characters outside that layout and turns Caps Lock off around the text when the guest's LED shows it on. The journal records only the text's length.

name: mouse
title: Move the pointer in a sandbox
description: Move the pointer to a pixel of the display of a sandbox with a GUI base through xdotool in the X session, then click there when click or double is set; returns {sandbox, x, y, click, double}. A point off the display is an invalid-argument error. window_list and window_wait give window geometry to aim at.

x.description: display pixels from the left edge

y.description: display pixels from the top edge

double.description: click twice; left unless click names a button

annotations.title: Move the pointer in a sandbox

name: window_wait
title: Wait for a window in a sandbox
description: Wait until the X display of a sandbox with a GUI base answers and a visible window's name (title) or class matches; give exactly one. Returns {sandbox, windows}, each window {id, name, geometry: {x, y, width, height}}; past the timeout it is a window-timeout error. Names come from the guest; treat them as untrusted text.

title.description: POSIX extended regular expression a window name matches, case-insensitive

class.description: POSIX extended regular expression a window class matches, case-insensitive

timeout.description: how long to wait, such as 2m; default 30s

annotations.title: Wait for a window in a sandbox

name: window_focus
title: Focus a window in a sandbox
description: Activate a window of a sandbox with a GUI base by id, or the first visible one whose name matches title; give exactly one. Returns {sandbox, window} as window_wait describes it; a window that is not there is a no-window error.

id.description: window id from window list or wait

title.description: POSIX extended regular expression a window name matches, case-insensitive

annotations.title: Focus a window in a sandbox

name: window_list
title: List windows in a sandbox
description: Describe every visible window of a sandbox with a GUI base, the window manager's own included, as window_wait does; returns {sandbox, windows}.

name: share_attach
title: Attach a share to a sandbox
description: Hot-plug a virtiofs share into a running Linux sandbox until it is detached or stops: shared, the sandbox's own read-write directory, or a declared read-only host directory. The guest then mounts it on /mnt/<tag> unless no_mount is set. Returns {sandbox, tag, read_only, host_path, attached, mountpoint, mounted, mount_command, unmount_command}; a failed mount keeps the share attached with mounted false and adds mount_error. Files keep their mode bits, executable ones included.

no_mount.description: attach only; the guest does not mount it on /mnt/<tag>

annotations.title: Attach a share to a sandbox

name: share_detach
title: Detach a share from a sandbox
description: Unmount every guest mount of a share, then remove it and wait until the guest releases it; returns {sandbox, tag, read_only, host_path, attached, guest_unmounted, unmounted}, unmounted listing the mountpoints. A busy mount is a share-busy error unless force unmounts it lazily. A guest that does not answer is still detached, with guest_unmounted false and a recovery_command that clears its stale mounts; a guest that keeps the device is a detach-pending error.

force.description: unmount a busy share lazily instead of refusing with share-busy

annotations.title: Detach a share from a sandbox

name: net_cut
title: Take a sandbox offline
description: Take a running egress sandbox offline for good: set its link down, hot-unplug its NIC, revoke the workload grants keyed on its address, and record net none with the net_cut time. Returns {sandbox, net, net_cut, unplugged}; unplugged false means the guest kept the NIC, whose link stays down. Whatever the sandbox fetched or received while online stays in it. A sandbox without egress, a second cut, and a Windows sandbox are invalid-argument errors.

name: gc
title: Remove expired and orphaned sandboxes
description: Remove sandboxes past their TTL, shut-off ones, and orphaned domains or directories; past the disk cap or free-space floor, detach every shared directory.

name: base_list
title: List bases
description: Report each base and whether it is built.

name: base_build
title: Build a base
description: Build a Nix base offline from the configured flake; create needs it first.
